comments.concern: SizeAndPosition computes window width as Characters.Count * ItemWidthDip but never adds the TransientSurface Margin (24,24,24,16), so narrow accent bars are under-sized and the content gets clipped.
comments.detail: The inner surface reserves 24px left + 24px right of padding inside the window. The width path (contentWidthDip = count*48) ignores that 48px, while DescriptionMinWidthDip is 648 (= WPF's 600 + 48 margin), so the two code paths are inconsistent. Without the description row a short bar will lose ~one accent cell off the edge. The old WPF window used SizeToContent and never had to account for this manually.

comments.concern: Hard-coded layout magic numbers (RowHeightDip=92, DescriptionHeightDip=36, ItemWidthDip=48, DescriptionMinWidthDip=648) replace WPF's automatic SizeToContent measurement.
comments.detail: These constants silently encode the item template height, card border, font size and margins. If the ItemContainerStyle, FontSize, theme metrics or padding change, the bar will be clipped or over-sized with no compile-time signal. A ListView-measured or template-derived size (or at least a comment tying each constant to the XAML it mirrors) would be far less fragile.

comments.concern: SizeAndPosition mixes two different DPI sources: the top-left comes from Calculation using GetActiveDisplay().Dpi, but width/height use FlyoutWindowHelper.GetDpiScale(DisplayArea.GetFromPoint(coordinates)).
comments.detail: On a mixed-DPI multi-monitor setup the monitor the anchor math targets (active/caret monitor) and the monitor DisplayArea.GetFromPoint resolves from the computed physical point can be different, so the size DPI and the position DPI disagree — the classic double-scaling / wrong-monitor mis-placement the added unit tests are meant to guard against, but which they can't catch because they only test the pure Calculation math, not this glue.

comments.concern: Replacing the synchronous Application.Current.Dispatcher.Invoke with RunOnUiThread (inline when HasThreadAccess, else TryEnqueue) assumes the low-level keyboard-hook callbacks always arrive on the UI thread.
comments.detail: InitHook is called from the PowerAccent ctor (UI thread), so WH_KEYBOARD_LL callbacks are pumped on the UI thread and inline execution preserves the WPF ordering. But this is now an unstated invariant: if the hook is ever installed off the UI thread, TryEnqueue defers the accent injection asynchronously, and the injected character / arrow key can race the trigger key-up. The comment acknowledges this but there is no assertion; worth making the invariant explicit/enforced.

comments.concern: The delayed render uses Task.Delay(...).ContinueWith(..., TaskScheduler.FromCurrentSynchronizationContext()), which depends on a DispatcherQueueSynchronizationContext being current when ShowToolbar runs.
comments.detail: Program.Main installs a DispatcherQueueSynchronizationContext inside Application.Start on the UI thread; the migration works only because ShowToolbar executes on that thread. This coupling between Program.cs's SynchronizationContext setup and Core's ContinueWith is subtle and undocumented — if the sync context is ever null (e.g. callback path changes), OnChangeDisplay would fire on a thread-pool thread and touch WinUI off-thread.

comments.concern: The comment claims a never-activated SW_SHOWNA overlay will follow live light/dark theme switches and retint the acrylic automatically, which is not guaranteed for a hidden/never-activated WinUI window.
comments.detail: WinUI re-resolves {ThemeResource} brushes on a theme change for realized, shown content; a window that is only ever shown non-activated and hidden between uses may not receive the settings/theme change notification while hidden. This should be verified on a real dark<->light switch while the module is idle, otherwise the popup can appear with stale theme colors on first summon after a switch.

comments.concern: GetRawCoordinatesFromCaret is exercised by 4 of the new unit tests but is not called anywhere in production (GetDisplayCoordinates only calls GetRawCoordinatesFromPosition), and unlike the Position variant it applies no DPI factor.
comments.detail: The tests give a false sense of coverage for a caret-placement feature that isn't wired in, and if it is ever hooked up it will mis-place at non-100% scaling because window size is treated as DIP while caret/screen are physical, with no dpi multiply. Either wire it up correctly (with DPI) or drop the dead method and its tests.

comments.concern: The Terminate fallback path (Environment.Exit(0) when the DispatcherQueue is null or draining) skips MainWindow.Dispose, so SaveUsageInfo is not called and usage statistics are silently dropped.
comments.detail: This is called out in the comment as acceptable, but it's a behavior regression from the WPF OnClosed path which always saved. Since the exit signal can arrive right after launch (runner death / disable), frequent-character ordering could intermittently fail to persist. Worth confirming this race is rare enough to accept, or persisting usage info incrementally rather than only on shutdown.

comments.concern: Removing `using System.Management;` is unrelated to the Quick Accent WinUI 3 migration and looks like scope creep in an otherwise module-scoped PR.
comments.detail: The using is genuinely unused (no System.Management references remain), so the change is harmless, but bundling an unrelated Settings.UI.Library edit into a module migration PR makes the diff harder to review and bisect. It likely belongs in a separate cleanup change (or was pulled in to silence an AOT/trim warning, which should be stated).

comments.concern: Accessibility exposes only AutomationProperties.AutomationId (QuickAccentCharacterList / QuickAccentDescription) and a hard-coded window title 'Quick Accent'; there is no localized AutomationProperties.Name for screen readers.
comments.detail: AutomationId is for automation/test identification, not for what Narrator announces. The PR states no new localizable strings, but a non-activating overlay with no accessible Name may announce nothing meaningful. Confirm the accent list/description are actually reachable/announced, and that the literal window title matching ColorPicker is the agreed pattern.

comments.concern: PublishAot=true is newly enabled for the Quick Accent UI (mirroring PowerDisplay) together with CommunityToolkit.Mvvm source generators, x:Bind and CsWinRT projections.
comments.detail: AOT/trim analyzers alone don't guarantee the app launches once ILC-compiled — reflection in telemetry, JSON settings serialization (SourceGenerationContext), or WinUIEx can fail only at runtime under AOT. Please confirm a Release/AOT-published build actually starts and shows the toolbar, not just that it compiles.

comments.concern: The launch path is hard-coded relative as `WinUI3Apps\PowerToys.PowerAccent.exe`, which relies on the runner's current working directory being the install root.
comments.detail: If the module interface is ever loaded with a different CWD, CreateProcess with a relative path will fail to find the exe. Other WinUI3Apps modules use the same pattern, so this is likely consistent, but it's worth confirming the runner resolves this relative to the module directory (or uses an absolute path) rather than the process CWD.

comments.concern: PowerToys.PowerAccentModuleInterface.dll is intentionally left in the install root while Core/Common/exe/KeyboardService move to WinUI3Apps\ — this split must match the actual harvested layout and the verify script.
comments.detail: The signing list, verify-installation-script.ps1 and the WiX/glob harvesting must all agree, otherwise signing fails or the installer ships an unsigned/missing binary. The module interface staying in root (runner-loaded) vs everything else under WinUI3Apps is a correct but easy-to-desync split — confirm all three sources list identical paths.

comments.concern: IsAlwaysOnTop is toggled true-on-show / false-on-hide to avoid pinning a discrete GPU awake, but it is set before Show() and there is no guarantee it is reset if an exception occurs between show and hide.
comments.detail: The hybrid-GPU mitigation (issue #34849) depends on IsAlwaysOnTop reliably returning to false whenever the overlay is dormant. If SizeAndPosition/Show throws, or a summon is interrupted, the flag could stick at true on a never-destroyed window and defeat the mitigation. Consider resetting it defensively (e.g. finally / on the hide path unconditionally).
